subject: Post-discovery: schedule ML/infra deep dive & attendee alignment

Subject: Post-discovery: schedule ML/infra deep dive & attendee alignment

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand Helio Health's primary goals for inference: lower per-token cost for batch claims processing, sub-150ms tail latency for the triage service, and strict data isolation for PHI. High-level recap below so we're aligned before we lock a follow-up: 

- Current priority: pilot inference for claim-normalization and redaction pipeline (60k QPS bursts)
- Success metric: 30% reduction in per-call cost vs their current hosted endpoints; latency SLO for triage path
- Security asks: SOC2 audit evidence, KMS integration, retention controls

Next suggested step: schedule a 60–90 minute ML/infra technical deep dive with our infra engineers and Helio's engineering leads. Goal: validate architecture, surface any blockers (data movement, keys, network), and produce a mutual action plan with dependencies and owners.

Proposed agenda (60–90m):
1) 5m — quick intros and objectives
2) 15m — Helio architecture & volume profile (you + Priya)
3) 20–30m — Redwood runtime: routing, batching, caching, quantization options (Marcus)
4) 15–25m — deployment model decision: Dedicated vs Private (security + ops) (Evelyn + Ben)
5) 10m — action items & next steps / mutual action plan

Suggested windows (all PT):
- Tue Nov 17: 10:00–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Wed Nov 18: 09:00–10:30 or 15:00–16:30

Attendees we recommend from Redwood: Marcus Lin (serving/runtime), Evelyn Hart (ops & private deployments), Ben Carter (solutions lead). From Helio we expect Samir and Priya. If those windows don't work, send two alternative 60–90m slots and we'll mirror in our calendars.

I've attached a short precall checklist and an initial mutual action plan (stub) to help Helio prioritize what to bring (sample data volumes, representative prompts, network topology).

Thanks — happy to tweak the agenda.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
